title: Homotopically flat sheaf dg resolutions compute derived extension
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of associative unital dg $\mathcal O$-algebras, with left dg modules, homotopies, shifts, localization and ordinary balanced tensor as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A left dg $\mathcal A$-module $H$ is called homotopically flat over $\mathcal A$ if $T\otimes_{\mathcal A}H$ is acyclic for every acyclic right dg $\mathcal A$-module $T$. Here a right module has $d(ta)=d(t)a+(-1)^{|t|}t\,d(a)$, the tensor is the sheafified direct-sum total balanced tensor, and acyclic means all underlying cohomology sheaves vanish. Equivalently, $-\otimes_{\mathcal A}H$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms of right dg modules.

Every possibly unbounded left dg $\mathcal A$-module $M$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $h:H\to M$ with $H$ homotopically flat over $\mathcal A$ and flat as a graded $\mathcal A$-module (graded flat means that tensoring with it is exact on right graded module sheaves). For any homomorphism $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ of sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebras, let $L=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}^{\mathbf L}-$ be the universal left derived extension and $\varepsilon_H:L(H)\to\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}H$ its comparison, which exist by [lem-sfb-ringed-dg-scalar-adjunction]. For every graded-flat homotopically flat $H$, $\varepsilon_H$ is an isomorphism in $D_X(\mathcal B)$. These comparison isomorphisms are natural for dg module maps between such $H$. No flatness over $\mathcal O$ of $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal B$ or $M$, and no boundedness, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0FSH (lemma-resolve), Tag 0FSI (lemma-acyclic-good), Tag 0FSC (lemma-good-admissible-ses), and Tag 0FTF (lemma-derived-tensor-product). Left modules by opposite algebras. The source good resolutions have the stated two flatness properties; the computation for the class defined by these two properties follows by the same cone argument of 0FSI and 0FTF, dropping only the unused universal-base-change property of good modules.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal P$ for the graded-flat homotopically flat left modules. First record the cone calculation. For a right-module map $g$, $C(g)\otimes_{\mathcal A}H\cong C(g\otimes1)$ by the identity on its two summands. For a left-module map $f$, the map $T\otimes C(f)\to C(1\otimes f)$ is $t\otimes(n,m)\mapsto(t\otimes n,(-1)^{|t|}t\otimes m)$. Substitution in $d(t\otimes m)=dt\otimes m+(-1)^{|t|}t\otimes dm$ verifies both formulas and their inverses. The same signs send homotopies to homotopies. The cone short exact sequence and its cohomology sequence say that a map is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when its cone is acyclic. Consequently the stated acyclic-tensor condition for $H$ implies preservation of all quasi-isomorphisms of right modules. Conversely apply preservation to $T\to0$ for acyclic $T$. This proves the equivalence in the statement without a flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0FSI (lemma-acyclic-good), cone argument; explicit tensor signs from section-dg-bimodules

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-good-resolutions], in its left-module form, every left dg $\mathcal A$-module $M$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $h:H\to M$ with $H$ good. The first two conditions of goodness for a left module say exactly that $-\otimes_{\mathcal A}H$ is exact on graded right module sheaves and that $T\otimes_{\mathcal A}H$ is acyclic for every acyclic right dg module $T$. Hence $H\in\mathcal P$, which proves the resolution clause of the statement; the base-change condition of goodness is not used. The right-module form of the same node gives, for every right dg module $N$, a quasi-isomorphism $R\to N$ with $R$ good, so that $R\otimes_{\mathcal A}C$ is acyclic for every acyclic left dg module $C$. The conventions of that node (Leibniz rules, sheafified balanced direct-sum total tensor, underlying cohomology sheaves) are those of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization] and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]; the open site of $X$ is small in the universes fixed by the statement.

source.place: Tag 0FSH (lemma-resolve), with Tags 0FSF (remark-sheaf-graded-sets) and 0FSG (lemma-free-graded-module-good) in its first proof; conditions (1) and (2) of good modules

proof.text: An acyclic homotopically flat left module $C$ tensors acyclically with every right dg module $N$. Indeed choose a right resolution $R\to N$ from step 2, so $R$ is homotopically flat and $E=C(R\to N)$ is acyclic. The complex $R\otimes_{\mathcal A}C$ is acyclic by right homotopical flatness and acyclicity of $C$; $E\otimes_{\mathcal A}C$ is acyclic by left homotopical flatness and acyclicity of $E$. The cone identity of step 1 and the cohomology sequence of its degreewise split cone sequence imply $N\otimes_{\mathcal A}C$ is acyclic. This is precisely the argument of lemma-acyclic-good; it uses only the two tensor-acyclicity properties, not the stronger requirement of remaining good after all base changes.

source.place: Tag 0FSI (lemma-acyclic-good), proof (1), with opposite module sides

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism $f:P\to P'$ between objects of $\mathcal P$, its cone $C$ is acyclic by the sheaf dg cone lemma. Its graded module is $P'\oplus P[1]$, so it is graded-flat. For acyclic right $T$, the cone identity $T\otimes C\cong C(T\otimes f)$ and the cohomology sequence show acyclicity, since both $T\otimes P$ and $T\otimes P'$ are acyclic. Thus $C$ is also homotopically flat. Step 3 with $N=\mathcal B$ gives $\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}C$ acyclic, and step 1 identifies it with $C(\mathcal B\otimes f)$. Therefore ordinary extension followed by localization, $F:K_X(\mathcal A)\to D_X(\mathcal B)$, inverts every quasi-isomorphism between objects of $\mathcal P$. It is a functor on the homotopy category by the homotopy calculation in step 1.

source.place: Tag 0FTF (lemma-derived-tensor-product), proof, cone test for preservation

proof.text: Apply the existing sheaf dg homotopy-system theorem to the open site of $X$. Its right-module assertion applies to left $\mathcal A$-modules through the graded opposite algebra $\mathcal A^{\rm op}$, with $a^{\rm op}b^{\rm op}=(-1)^{|a||b|}(ba)^{\rm op}$ and $a^{\rm op}m=(-1)^{|a||m|}ma$; substitution shows that this matches the Leibniz rules, the Koszul-signed shifted action, the graded homotopies and the cones of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. It gives the triangulated homotopy category and the quasi-isomorphisms $W$ with a right calculus of fractions and two-out-of-three; these are exactly the hypotheses required by the following categorical tools. By steps 2 and 4, $\mathcal P$ resolves every object and $F$ inverts its $W$-arrows. Apply the resolving-class essential-constancy theorem: the denominator diagram $W/X\to D_X(\mathcal B)$ is essentially constant for every $X$, with its identity leg invertible when $X\in\mathcal P$. The pointwise-Kan bridge gives a limit of the structured-arrow diagram with this same identity leg as comparison. The pointwise right-Kan theorem then assembles these limits into a universal left derived pair $(L',\varepsilon')$; in particular $\varepsilon'_P$ is invertible for all $P\in\mathcal P$. This applies to dg modules as a category in its own right, not to ordinary complexes in the abelian category of graded modules.

source.place: Tag 0FTF (lemma-derived-tensor-product), invoking derived.tex Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual criterion; expanded with existing general categorical nodes

proof.text: The pair $(L,\varepsilon)$ specified in the statement exists by the scalar-adjunction node. Its universal property and that of $(L',\varepsilon')$ give unique maps $u:L\to L'$ and $v:L'\to L$ satisfying $\varepsilon'\circ(uQ)=\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon\circ(vQ)=\varepsilon'$. Their composites are identities by the uniqueness clauses of the same two universal properties. Hence $\varepsilon_P=\varepsilon'_P u_{QP}$ is an isomorphism for every $P\in\mathcal P$. For a dg map $f:P\to P'$ between such modules, naturality of the specified $\varepsilon$ is the equation $\varepsilon_{P'}L(Qf)=Q(\mathcal B\otimes f)\varepsilon_P$. This is exactly the required naturality of the comparison isomorphisms. Throughout, flatness has been used only over the graded algebra $\mathcal A$, so no flatness over $\mathcal O$ of either algebra or $M$ has entered.

source.place: Tag 0FTF (lemma-derived-tensor-product), comparison with the universal derived extension; uniqueness and naturality
